heading: EXT. BOCCE COURT - SUNSET LODGE RETIREMENT HOME - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: EXT. BOCCE COURT - SUNSET LODGE RETIREMENT HOME - LATE AFTERNOON
A clay court framed by weathered boards, bordered by hydrangeas gone brown at the edges.
The sun is low and gold.
A radio plays something slow from an open window.
CONSTANTINE "CONNIE" PAPADAKIS, seventies, white shirt, braces, crouches with a green ball cupped in his palm.
Across the court ELMER HOLLINGSWORTH, seventies, in a flat cap, leans on a cane and studies the pallino.
Between them, seated on a folding chair with a clipboard, VIOLA REARDON, eighties, referee, in a lavender cardigan, watches both with equal indifference.
Connie rolls.
The ball curves, slows, kisses the pallino, and stops.
Elmer's cane taps once against the boards.
Viola writes down a number without a word.
Elmer picks up his own ball, weighs it, sets his feet, and rolls.
It rolls wide, wobbles, and dies a hand's breadth from the line.
Connie nods, folds his arms, and gazes at the sky.
Viola capitalises something on her clipboard.
Neither man looks at the other.
Connie takes his second ball from the bucket and turns it over twice, and Elmer, from the far end, produces a handkerchief and blots his forehead with the slow ceremony of a man not in a hurry.
Viola lowers the clipboard and takes a long sip of her iced tea.
Four to two.
units.name: VIOLA

units.text: Thank you, Viola.
units.name: CONNIE

units.text: Two's not bad.
units.name: ELMER

units.text: It's two.
units.name: VIOLA

units.text: Connie rolls again.
Another kiss, another stop.
Elmer watches it settle and for a moment his cane trembles.
He reaches into his cardigan, fingers a folded photograph, then thinks better of it and tucks it back.
You all right, Elmer?
units.name: CONNIE

units.text: Sun's in my eyes.
units.name: ELMER

units.text: Sun's behind you.
units.name: CONNIE

units.text: Then it's the other one.
units.name: ELMER

units.text: Viola caps her pen.
She rises, brushes clay from her cardigan, and walks the length of the court at her own pace, bends, and measures with a short string.
She straightens.
Game.
units.name: VIOLA

units.text: Good game.
units.name: CONNIE

units.text: Hm.
units.name: ELMER

units.text: They shake hands over the boards, a dry brief shake.
Viola gathers the balls into the bucket.
Connie holds the gate for Elmer.
Elmer goes through it and does not say thank you, and Connie does not seem to expect it, and the radio drifts on.
